scope: Source-note finalization for canonical Chapter Φ and Interlude Φ; not a substantive prose rewrite or blanket factual clearance.
status: Existing reference checks completed at the documented access level; two historical bookmarks added. Manual prose issues remain open.
method: Cited passages, bibliographic identity and recoverable locators checked. Abstract-only and metadata-only checks explicitly identified. Proofs were not independently rederived. Research uses primary texts, author manuscripts, official documentation and identified scholarly interpretation.

manual_prose_followups.anchor: That is the boy’s predicament on the plane, made exact / We can’t step outside arithmetic
manual_prose_followups.issue: Gödel’s formal result does not make the memoir analogy exact or forbid external mathematical reasoning.
manual_prose_followups.action: Keep the image as an analogy and narrow the categorical language in the manual prose pass.

manual_prose_followups.anchor: The reasoning “if I’m consistent, then G is true” can be carried out inside the system
manual_prose_followups.issue: Formal derivation concerns the sentence G, not an internal general truth predicate.
manual_prose_followups.action: Use “if the theory is consistent, then G” for the formal implication.

manual_prose_followups.anchor: Chapter 1 will start from exactly this space
manual_prose_followups.issue: Hilbert space with its defined structure is not identical to unrestricted prephysical possibility.
manual_prose_followups.action: Adjust the bridge to distinguish the formal physical analogy from the conjecture.

manual_prose_followups.issue: Signed velocity integrates to displacement; speed integrates to distance travelled.
manual_prose_followups.action: Change distance to displacement or explicitly limit the example to motion without reversal.

manual_prose_followups.issue: Gödel and Hilbert spoke in related Königsberg meetings, not necessarily one conference session sequence; Smith distinguishes public address and later radio recording.
manual_prose_followups.action: Prefer “at the associated Königsberg meetings” and keep the radio/public-address distinction if precise chronology is retained.

manual_prose_followups.anchor: Nodes and Edges / Two conditions seem to matter
manual_prose_followups.issue: Anderson is not a source for a universal two-condition emergence rule or a line-graph mechanism; temperature as mere jostling is a simplification.
manual_prose_followups.action: Retain as the author’s heuristic and qualify any universal physical assertion.

manual_prose_followups.anchor: Knowing What We Think We Know / confounder
manual_prose_followups.issue: Prediction without mechanistic explanation is not automatically luck, and an unexplained regularity is not necessarily confounding.
manual_prose_followups.action: Preserve the stopped-clock lesson while separating epistemic luck, induction and confounding.

notes.previous_note: Solomon Feferman, [The nature and significance of Gödel’s incompleteness theorems](https://math.stanford.edu/~feferman/papers/Godel-IAS.pdf) (2006), pp. 10–11. This historical account by a Gödel editor documents von Neumann’s response to the Königsberg announcement and his letter of 20 November 1930. Gödel’s paper, received on 17 November, proved the first theorem and announced the second.
notes.final_note: Feferman, [“The nature and significance of Gödel’s incompleteness theorems”](https://math.stanford.edu/~feferman/papers/Godel-IAS.pdf), pp. 10–11: von Neumann’s letter of 20 November 1930 and Gödel’s prior submission, received 17 November. The 1931 paper proved the first theorem and announced the second with a proof sketch.
notes.verification: Gödel editor Feferman’s historical discussion, pp. 10–11; Gödel manuscript’s received date and proposition XI announcement.
notes.scope_limits: Not a claim that the original 1931 publication supplied the later full proof of the second theorem.

notes.previous_note: Solomon Feferman, [The nature and significance of Gödel's incompleteness theorems](https://math.stanford.edu/~feferman/papers/Godel-IAS.pdf) (2006). Discussion following the incompleteness theorems. A stronger consistent, effective arithmetical theory can settle additional statements while remaining incomplete; no theorem about civil society follows automatically. The "turtles" reading is the author's.
notes.final_note: Feferman, [“The nature and significance of Gödel’s incompleteness theorems”](https://math.stanford.edu/~feferman/papers/Godel-IAS.pdf), pp. 4–9. Stronger consistent, effectively axiomatized arithmetical theories remain subject to incompleteness. The extension to human institutions and the passenger’s predicament is an analogy.
notes.verification: Feferman statements of incompleteness and discussion of stronger systems, pp. 4–9.
notes.scope_limits: Does not show that all guarantees require larger systems or that arithmetic cannot be studied from a metatheory. Those stronger claims remain a prose issue.

In the four-spoke star, all six pairs of spokes share the hub, so its line graph is the complete graph on four vertices. This verifies the example; the emergence interpretation remains the author’s.
notes.final_note: NetworkX Developers, [“line_graph”](https://networkx.org/documentation/stable/reference/generated/networkx.generators.line.line_graph.html), definition for undirected graphs (accessed 15 October 2026). Edges become vertices, adjacent when they share an endpoint. The four-spoke star therefore yields a complete four-vertex graph; the emergence interpretation is the author’s.
notes.verification: Official implementation documentation’s definition inspected; four-spoke star has six pairs sharing its hub, independently checked.
notes.scope_limits: The transformation is a mathematical redescription, not evidence of a physical emergence mechanism.

notes.previous_note: Silvanus P. Thompson, [Calculus Made Easy](https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/33283/pg33283-images.html) (1914), Macmillan and Co. Chapters VIII and XVII–XIX. notes.previous_note: John Preskill, [Quantum Information, Chapter 2: Foundations I: States and Ensembles](https://ilorentz.org/quantumcomputers/literature/preskill_2_update.pdf) (July 2015), §§2.1, 2.3 and 2.4.1, for pure states, measurement probabilities, density operators and entanglement; John von Neumann, [Mathematical Foundations of Quantum Mechanics](https://www.jstor.org/stable/j.ctt1wq8zhp), originally published in German in 1932, especially chapter II, “Abstract Hilbert Space.” A vector represents a pure state, up to overall phase; general states require density operators. Neither source establishes prephysical possibility space.

notes.previous_note: Oleg Mazonka and Alex Kolodin, [A Simple Multi-Processor Computer Based on Subleq](https://arxiv.org/abs/1106.2593) (2011), abstract and §2; Matthew Cook, [Universality in Elementary Cellular Automata](https://content.wolfram.com/sites/13/2023/02/15-1-1.pdf) (2004), _Complex Systems_ 15(1): 1–40, especially the introduction and construction; Cook, [A Concrete View of Rule 110 Computation](https://arxiv.org/abs/0906.3248) (2009), abstract. SUBLEQ branches when subtraction yields a nonpositive result. Rule 110 uses a cell and its two neighbors. Universality concerns computable functions under idealized resource assumptions; Cook’s construction uses specially arranged, unbounded backgrounds. A finite implementation remains limited by its physical resources.
notes.final_note: Oleg Mazonka and Alex Kolodin, [“A Simple Multi-Processor Computer Based on Subleq”](https://arxiv.org/abs/1106.2593) (2011), §2; Matthew Cook, [“Universality in Elementary Cellular Automata”](https://content.wolfram.com/sites/13/2023/02/15-1-1.pdf), _Complex Systems_ 15 (2004): 1–40, and [“A Concrete View of Rule 110 Computation”](https://arxiv.org/abs/0906.3248) (2009), abstract. SUBLEQ branches on a nonpositive result. Universality assumes unbounded resources; Cook’s construction uses specially arranged infinite backgrounds.
notes.verification: SUBLEQ paper §2 instruction semantics; Cook 2004 introduction and local three-cell update rule; Cook 2009 abstract explicitly specifies repeating left/right backgrounds and encoded computation.
notes.scope_limits: Universality proofs not rederived. Finite hardware cannot supply unbounded tape/time; computable does not mean feasible.
